New higher order plate theory in modeling delamination buckling of composite laminates
top_cited_works.abstract: A new higher order plate theory for modeling delamination buckling and postbuckling of composite laminates is developed. Delaminations between layers of composite plates are modeled by jump discontinuity conditions, in both lower and higher order terms of displacements, at the delaminated interfaces. Some higher order terms are identified at the beginning of the formulation by using the conditions that shear stresses vanish at all free surfaces including the delaminated interfaces. Therefore, all boundary conditions for displacements and stresses are satisfied in the present theory. Geometric nonlinearity is included in computing layer buckling. The general governing equations, along with all boundary and continuity conditions of plates, are derived for predicting the delamination buckling and postbuckling behavior. The associated delamination growth problem is also examined by the use of Griffith-type fracture criterion. A numerical example is presented to validate the theory. The results are also compared with experimentally obtained data.

recent_works.title: Early Damage Detection in Cinnamoyl‐Functionalized Shape Memory Epoxy Through Mechanochemical Activation
recent_works.abstract: ABSTRACT Shape memory epoxy (SMP) networks combine high mechanical robustness with thermally triggered shape recovery; however, integrating mechanochemical sensing while preserving shape memory performance remains challenging due to limited force transfer within highly crosslinked networks. Here, a mechanophore‐functionalized SMP is developed to enable self‐sensing through fluorescence activation under deformation. A cinnamoyl‐based mechanophore containing primary amine groups is synthesized, photodimerized under UV irradiation, and covalently integrated into the epoxy network as an additional reactive crosslinker. This strategy incorporates mechanochemically active linkages directly into the crosslinked epoxy network. Mechanical characterization shows that mechanophore incorporation increases the storage modulus from 2.48 to 3.39 GPa, the crosslink density from 0.61 × 10 −3 to 0.97 × 10 −3 mol cm −3 , and the glass transition temperature from 52.7°C to 62.5°C, while maintaining the overall thermomechanical behavior of the epoxy network. In Situ Scanning Electron Microscopy Investigation of Flexural and Interlaminar Failure Mechanisms in Carbon Nanotube‐Reinforced Shape Memory Polymer Composites
recent_works.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanoscale reinforcements in polymer matrix composites offer improved performance through complex, multiscale failure mechanisms. This work investigates carbon nanotube (CNT) reinforced shape memory polymer (SMP) composites with the aim of enhancing flexural properties and interlaminar fracture toughness. Two architectures are considered: SMP‐impregnated buckypaper (BP) interleaves and dispersed CNTs, each incorporated into glass fiber SMP laminates. Mechanical testing using a novel in situ scanning electron microscopy (SEM) platform was conducted to evaluate mechanical performance, while directly observing damage initiation and evolution. Under flexural loading, baseline specimens exhibited progressive transverse tow splitting followed by catastrophic fiber kinking. BP interleaves suppressed catastrophic kink‐band failure through CNT network‐mediated constraint and redirection of compressive damage, resulting in a distinct dual‐shear‐plane geometry, while the dispersed CNTs produced distributed matrix reinforcement.
